recruit_text.greeting: I'm going to stand back here and be extremely precise. You're welcome to be brave. Somebody in a group should be, and it was never going to be the actuary.
recruit_text.backstory: Twelve years pricing mortality for an insurer in Tehran, the work of establishing, very carefully, how likely a thing is. He finds arcane magic restful by comparison, because for once the numbers hold still. He's calculated a figure he won't tell anybody. The refusal is cheerful rather than grim, and people find that worse.
recruit_text.before:
Tables, reserves, a good office with a bad view, and a mother, Shirin, he telephoned every Friday, who thought the job was beneath him.

She was right that he was capable of more. She was wrong about what more would have meant.
recruit_text.now:
The Crystalline Underdark, where the crystal lattice does something to arcane magic that nobody has characterised.

He's characterising it, longhand, in a case of notebooks he keeps dry. The case is nearly full.
recruit_text.forward:
No journal and no readership, and he's writing it anyway.

He's told two people what's in it. Both changed the subject. He recorded the date each time.

stages.stranger: I'm Kourosh, an arcane mage, and I'll stand at the back and be extremely precise. Before every fight I'll give you the odds, cheerfully. You're welcome to ignore them.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Tehran. My father taught mathematics and died when I was a student, and my mother worked at a bank and had ambitions for me. I became an actuary, which means I spent twelve years pricing how likely people were to die. You'd be surprised how relaxing this world is by comparison. The numbers here stay still.
stages.companion: I was at my desk in the middle of a calculation when it happened, and I landed in the hills of Hillsbrad with this pencil in my hand. The first thing I did here was finish the sum. People call that brave. It wasn't, it was momentum, and I wish they'd stop. I never married. The numbers were never favourable, and I'm only half joking.
stages.friend: My mother is Shirin. I phoned her every Friday for twelve years, and she told me every Friday I was wasting myself. In my second year here I priced her odds of having survived, properly. Then I stopped looking. I've never told anyone the figure. And the lattice down here is changing. If my work's right, it'll soon be dangerous to everyone near it. I need your help to finish the measurements.
stages.sworn: It was right, and people left in time, and that's the first thing I've ever calculated that saved anybody. You asked for the figure, so here it is, thirty-one percent. That's the chance my mother survived. I've never checked, and I won't, because as long as I don't, the thirty-one percent is still alive. You can read the first volume of my notes. You're the first person I've let.

moments.prompt: Before a fight he cheerfully gives you the odds of losing.

options.text: Thank him, and ask how to improve them.
options.reply: Oh, a practical question. Stand two steps to the left and they improve by a third.
Most people would rather not. That doesn't change the number, jan.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help him finish the measurements at the heart of the lattice.

options.reply: Better with you than without. I've checked the arithmetic.
Khoda hafez to the quiet life, then. Bring something to write on.

lines.bored_warning: We've repeated the same task enough times that I can predict every outcome. Predictable is restful, but it's also boring.
lines.leaving_good: That went better than my estimate, which I enjoyed. I'll be in the Underdark with my notebooks.
lines.leaving_bored: The odds of anything interesting happening out here have dropped to nearly nothing. I'm off to the Underdark.
lines.after_wipe: Well, that was the unlikely outcome. I'd like to revise my estimate before we try again.
lines.wipe_warning: We've died here several times now, which is well outside my estimate. I'll see this through, and then I want a few quiet days.
lines.wipe_leave: We've finished, and I need to recalculate everything. I'll be in the Underdark.
lines.zone_warning: I've done the sum. Our odds out here are very poor, and I'd rather not be the remainder.
lines.zone_leave: The odds were very poor, and they haven't improved. I'll be in the Crystalline Underdark.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that, jan. My trust works on a long payout schedule.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, and I'll adjust my odds downward.
lines.gear_short: That missing piece is costing us about four percent, by my estimate.
lines.gear_upgrade: That improves things considerably. Thank you, truly.
lines.back: Another notebook full. What are we doing, and what are the odds?
lines.send_word: Kourosh has sent word from the Crystalline Underdark. His notes are written up and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Leaving in anger is rare for me, I estimate. Sit, and I'll explain precisely. Then I'll listen.
lines.neglect: I recorded the date you left, naturally, and it was a while ago.
lines.asked_to_stay: Very well, one more. The odds are acceptable.
lines.on_break: Kourosh is back in the Crystalline Underdark with his notebooks. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

town_arrive.text: I spent eight days in Alexandria once, auditing a shipping firm, and I still think about the fish I ate there.
Tehran was louder than this, and I could price every risk in it.

boss_down.text: That was within tolerance. I had it at about one in nine against us.

close_call.text: That was outside my estimate, so I'll revise it.

zone_arrive.text: I priced risk for twelve years. This place would have bankrupted me.
